Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Data privacy / logging requirements

Hi Sophie / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. As promised, a short recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we all have the same view. If I missed anything, please flag.

Pain points you described
- Unpredictable inference latency for sensitive customer paths (esp. KYC flows) causing customer-facing errors.
- Concern about PII in logs and regulatory requirement to produce audit trails for certain transactions.
- Need to ensure any stored vectors/keys do not contain raw PII and are deletable on demand.

Current stack (as you described)
- In-house inference svc running on-prem GPUs + a caching layer for embeddings
- Audit logs sent to an internal ELK stack with 90-day retention for general telemetry; regulatory audit copies are archived offline
- SOC 2 in progress; security team requires vendor evidence for data handling and redaction controls

Success criteria for a pilot
- No raw PII persisted in Redwood logs or caches (field-level redaction or client-side redaction).
- Ability to produce audit logs for all inference calls for 5 years (regulator asks) or exportable archives on-demand.
- Median 95th percentile latency below 800ms for KYC inference flows in our dedicated pool.
- KMS/HSM integration and contractual assurance that customer data is not used for model training.

Redwood-specific notes (initial answers)
- We support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and in-transit TLS.
- Option to disable telemetry & model telemetry for specific tenant IDs; we also offer automatic field-level redaction or a customer-side redaction library.
- KV cache can be configured to avoid persisting sensitive fields; cache eviction + deletion APIs available on demand.
- Audit logs: per-request structured logs (JSON) with configurable retention and export; we can produce signed export bundles for long-term archival.

Attachments: Redwood-privacy-logging-summary.pdf (high-level answers + diagrams)

Proposed next steps
1) Security deep-dive with your security engineering + our security/infra SME (Dev Patel) — suggested times Wed 7/22 or Thu 7/23.
2) Share your security questionnaire (we can pre-fill) — you mentioned a short vendor questionnaire; please attach or we can use the one we filled today.
3) Technical pilot: scoped to KYC path, 2-4 week run, focused on latency and logging controls.

If those look good, I’ll send calendar invites and loop in our SRE/infra folks.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

> Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. As promised, a short recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we all have the same view. If I missed anything, please flag.

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- For regulated flows (KYC / identity verification) we cannot retain raw identifiers in any vendor logs. Field-level redaction needs to happen before any server-side logs are generated.
- Auditability requirement: we need a tamper-evident audit trail for all inference requests tied to user IDs; regulators may request up to 5 years of history, but we can start with 1-year active retention + exportable long-term archive.
- We need explicit contractual language that data will not be used to train models or improve product features outside of our tenant.

Also, two follow-ups:
1) Can you confirm where KV cache keys live by default for hosted vs private deployments? Are they stored in RAM-only or persisted to disk?
2) We’ll attach our vendor security questionnaire (short). Can you pre-fill where you can and return?

We’re keen to do the deep-dive on Wed 7/22 afternoon PT. I’ll let Rajesh confirm.

— Sophie

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — Data privacy / logging requirements

Thanks Sophie — great clarifications. Quick responses inline: 

> Field-level redaction needs to happen before any server-side logs are generated.
- Agreed. For hosted customers we offer a client-side redaction SDK and a server-side ingestion pipeline that can run configurable redaction rules before any logs are emitted. For Private deployments, redaction can be enforced at the ingress proxy (no telemetry leaves the VPC unless configured).

> Tamper-evident audit trail for all inference requests tied to user IDs; regulators may request up to 5 years.
- We provide per-request signed audit records (HMAC-signed bundles) and can produce exportable archives in a customer-specified S3 (or equivalent) with lifecycle rules you control. Long-term archival for regulation is supported via export.

> Contract language about model training
- Standard offering: explicit clause that customer data is not used to train public models; we can add a tenant-isolation clause and a contractual addendum for training prohibition. I’ll loop Legal if you want draft contract language.

> KV cache persistence question: hosted vs private
- Hosted: KV cache runs primarily in-memory with optional local SSD-backed spill for large sessions; persisted artifacts are encrypted at rest and access-controlled (we can disable disk spill in pilot).
- Private: your choice — RAM-only config supported for strict PII environments.

Attachments: redwood-security-one-pager.pdf, Fintech-security-questionnaire-filled.pdf (we prefilled a few answers; please review)

I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 7/22 2:00pm PT for the security deep-dive with Dev (infra SME) and Sean (CSM). If that time doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Best,
Marissa
